Newlands Bark Stripping

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
The centuries old Newlands Forest is under threat from Bark strippers and unless something dramatic is done very soon it will collapse. Newlands Forest is extremely accessible from the M3 highway and bark strippers gain easy access at night, carrying sack loads out of the forest destroying 100's of year old trees. With big winter storms and years of severe drought the old trees are dying off. Assagai and Black Stink wood trees both protected trees are now virtually eradicated in the forest and SANPARKS have very limited resources to fight the scourge. Now volunteer groups like Take Back the Mountain have mounted night patrols to catch the strippers red handed and SANPARK wardens are working in the off times to try and stop this scourge

Summary:
In the last year stripping has ramped up and literally 1000’s of trees have been stripped. Strippers work along the rivers so the noise masks their activities. Its being run by highly organized gangs with the Sangomas going in and identifying the tress and making with arrows and then using young boys to carry out the sacks so if they get caught they wont get heavy sentences. Black Stinkwood carries R100 000 fine or 6 months in prison but the strippers are very hard to catch.

As indigenous forests shrink across the country, about 0.5% of South Africa's total land area is covered by natural forests, the demand far outweighs the supply and the pressure on a forest like Newlands, which is so easily accessible to the public, is enormous. The bark stripping has got completely out of hand and the bark is being shipped across the country to traditional medicine markets in the sack loads.


Further information:
Sadly as the 100 year old trees dies off the canopy of the forest is destroyed letting more light into the forest floor and the young saplings don't gro. Bark stripping has changed the nature of the forest and it's eco system is being destroyed. With more light on the floor of the forest alien vegetation invades, raising the risk of destroying the forest through fire. In May this year that came very close when the fire that destroyed the Jagger Library at UCT fortunately turned down onto the highway and burnt itself out, saving Newlands forest. Afro mountain forest cannot afford to burn, they take 100's of years to recover if ever.

SANPARKS doesn't have the finances or manpower to patrol Newlands so citizen groups like Newlands Conservation and Take Back The Mountain- a bunch of police type reservist are trying to raise awareness and support SANPARK Rangers. They have agreed to take us in. They hope by raising awareness that the uses of the forest will alert the rangers to any suspicious activity and the strippers will be caught. The only hope for Newlands is if citizen groups like Newlands Conservation that it educating the public, and also clearing up the litter and removing alien vegetation. Take Back The Mountain are volunteers who are armed and patrol the mountain to assist with security and offer the rangers more protection. Encountering armed gangs in the forest with pangas is what it boils down to. But these Capetonians are desperate to save this precious resource from the scourge of plant poachers. And the threat is very real, Botanists think it's just a matter of years before the whole eco system collapses

Extra Budget Items:
2 nights of accommodation in Cape Town. I will need two nights of accommodation for Masa in Cape Town. She will need to fly in at the end of Tuesday so she is able to work on Wednesday till 10pm Wed night and there is no ways she can start at 3am in JHB to get to Cape Town to start a 8.30 shoot. Also the logistics of getting into the forest where the trees are stripped is going to take more than the usual time. We are also hoping to get into the townships to film a traditional healer so its not like we can just hang out in one location. We will need Tue and Wed night accommodation to fly out on Thursday.

Script:


Script: We’re heading up Table mountain with SANPARK rangers and a group of volunteers from Take Back our mountain – our mission – a night patrol into Newlands Forest, to catch bark strippers in the act
Upsound
Script It’s quite a walk to get into the forest, and night is creeping in, but this is when bark strippers are the most active
Taahir Jjust keep quiet please so we can hear what is going on in the forest
Script: Harvesting bark for traditional medicine is an ancient practice, but in the last two years, it’s got completely out of control, and the forest is collapsing. Braving the cold winter nights and potential danger, Taahir Osman and his fellow volunteers, are bolstering SANPARKS efforts to patrol the forest day and night
Link Creeping along the boardwalk in the failing light can be quite tricky we’re trying not to alert the bark strippers of our presence
Script: The tension is palpable, the previous night two bark strippers were caught in the act, a rare event, only 5 have been arrested in the last 6 months. But it’s boosted everyone’s morale
Link He thinks he heard something but it just could be a bird or it might be a chopper
Script: The rangers are even camping out in the forest, often in their off time. Jake Daniels just come off day shift but spurred on by last nights arrest, joined the patrol
Masa: Have you ever encountered any danger yourself on one of these night patrols?

Robbie: “JAKE” , we've come across people also, some them staying overnight, in some of them being, you know, knives

Link We have been sitting here trying to hear any sounds of chopping but so far nothing yet, but the night is still young
Script: We’re heading down the ravine now where the most extensive bark stripping has happened, they use the sound of the river to mask the chopping
Taahir There is an X all along the areas that have been bark stripped. Some of it are fresh, it's almost an indication when they come strip, where to strip
Script: The forest is so dense with 100’s of paths, we could be walking right past them, and there are plenty of escape routes out onto the highway
Script: Several hours later the team emerged, sadly no arrests tonight
Upsound
Script Newlands Forest is one of Cape Town prized treasures, an ancient indigenous forest on the urban edge. 1000’s of people come here to relax, excise or mediate, it's a haven for children and dogs, and few have any idea how threatened it is
Francois” Ja the Japanese people do this as a therapy
Script: Arborist Francois Krige says Newlands Forest, is at a tipping point
Francois: a reasonable management plan for this forest would be no bark stripping for the next 200 years to allow it to recover.

Masa: Two hundred years?

Francois: Yes, forests do things very slowly.

Masa: So what does a tree that’s been stripped look like

Francois: This one has been stripped, it has no more intact bark around its base. It’s attempted to heal itself here, and then it was stripped again. It's tried to make a basal sucker to take over the role of the dead trunk and the existing root system, and even that is now being stripped. So this tree has tried repeatedly to survive and it's been repeatedly damaged.

Masa: As it stands, how far are we in protecting this forest

Francois: The rate of decline is accelerating rapidly within this forest. There's no signs of any sustainable harvesting programs being implemented, and the endgame is going to be the end of this forest.

PAUSE

Script: Bark protects a tree from insects and fungi, and acts as the nutrient supply line, stripping its bark, it's like ripping off our skin, the tree dries out and slowly dies

LINK: This is really tragic, what was once a thick dense canopy of ancient majestic trees, now looks like a war zone. And the last big winds blew over the dried out dead trees and as they fell, they took out the living trees around them
Franc:, the density of dead wood on the ground is way high if a fire came through the flames would be leaping up and destroying all these young trees.

Script: 80 to 100 year old trees are being stripped, five years ago there was a dense forest canopy overhead

LINK It’s easy to be outraged when you see the damage that bark stripping causes but the situation is much more complex. This forest is also a source of medicine for many many people and a multi-million rand industry

SCRIPT. Between 60 and 80% of the population uses traditional medicine, and bark is the most frequently used, representing one-third of plant material traded. Assegai - is used to treat stomach ailments, diarrhoea and as a blood purifier. And Boekenhout- for respiratory problems, sore throats, fevers, muscular and heart complaints, so there is little surprise, bark stripping spiked during the COVID pandemic
Roger “This one, they call Skilpad it comes from Knysna that this is very good, the skin problems
Masa for skin problems for eczema.

Script: Roger Campbell is one of thousands of informal traders and healers, that forms part of the extensive hidden network, stretching across the country. Botanist Professor Nomkwanda Makunga, of Stellenbosch University, says we all use herbal remedies in one form or another.

NOx large amounts of bark are being taken out of indigenous forests in South Africa to go for sale in herbal markets. And sometimes those practices are not necessarily conservative because the people who go collecting are sustaining their lives through selling that bark to traders that trade in these markets. The bark however, does hold medicinal value

Script She says it’s naïve to think it’s going to stop, because it represents a source of affordable medicine, and it’s not only the poor, and uneducated, who use it

Nox it becomes extremely tricky to try and regulate the trade. Healers and collectors are not necessarily the same people

Script: SANPARKS Section ranger for Newlands, Chamell Plium, has just come off night patrol. She wants far heavier penalties for bark stripping, as it’s a major environmental crime.
Chamell: it is as severe and if not more than a rhino poaching or abalone poaching because this is basically the ecosystem

Script: The majority of the mature Assegai and Boekenhout trees have been hit and they are moving onto new species.

CHamell: i….we've got about four trees just in this area .you've got mature trees as well as the young trees that's being bark stripped .

Script: If the tree is partially stripped, there is a chance that the bark will regrow and seal the tree, but when it’s ring barked, it has little chance of survival. As soon as they find a stripped tree, it’s painted with an organic sealant, as quickly as possible
Chamell “ We will be reapplying on this Boekenhout tree because it is not dead yet, the canopy is still alive and at the bottom we can see shoots coming out.
Script: Willem Boshoff of the Newlands Conservation, group is one of 100’s of concerned Capetonians, passionate about the forest, who realise the enormous task SANPARKS is up against
Williem We're sitting on a ticking time bomb. here, we're seeing the destruction happening and we need to fast track public involvement

Script: One of the things they itching to do is clear the alien vegetation which has crept into the indigenous forest, and presents an enormous fire hazard, with the fallen trees from bark stripping. There have been hacks, but not enough in Willem’s opinion

Willem Table Mountain National Park generates about 300 million rand in revenue a year, with an operating budget of 90 million rand. And we don't have a problem of other parks being cross-subsidised, but at the same time, we're saying if this park is being damaged and going backwards deploy those resources, get feet on the ground, have a strategy, guys make the budget available

Script: Only nought point 5% of the Western Cape’s indigenous forests are still intact, and in May, it was a close shave for Newlands, the wind swung driving the fire onto UCT, and down to the highway. Wildfires are destroying indigenous forests globally, and with the alien infestation in the heart of the Newlands, this ancient forest could ignite.

Willem “ Ja, we recently discovered an area where the guys are camping,
Link: “The bark strippers can hide away here for days in this dense forest, we have literally crawled through dense growth just to find it, PAUSE
but last night walked right past it
Script: Despite SANPARKS efforts to meet the traditional healer bodies and educating the youth, the harvesting has eclipsed their efforts.

Chamel:. We are going to be the generation that we have to look at that actually destroyed this forest. I implore everybody far and wide we should actually take action, and ask ourselves do we want to be that generation
